["Welcome to the Back Table Setup Skills Trainer module!

This module will cover the following skills:

Non-Sterile Equipment Positioning
Sterile Back Table Setup
Mayo Stand Setup.

In this tutorial, any instructions listed after “In VR:” should be completed within the training module.

Any information after “In Practice” is meant to provide additional information for real-world practice.

For today’s practice we will be setting up for a basic open appendectomy case.

Click NEXT to advance.","In VR:

Let’s start by moving some items from the case cart. Grab the large Back Table Pack and move it to the back table.","In VR:

Now, move the Sterile Gown pack to the Mayo Stand.","In VR:

Before opening any sterile items, ensure you, and anyone else in the room, are wearing a mask.","In VR:

Now that you are masked, open the back table pack to expose the contents.

When opening the Back Table Pack, open the left/right sides, the back side, and then the front side.","In Practice:

Spatial planning and awareness are very important when setting up the room. Make sure you have enough space on all sides of the table to properly open the pack.","In VR:

Next, open the gown overwrap. Open the left/right sides, the back side, and then the front side.","In VR:

Now, grab the sterile gloves from the case cart and open them onto the gown overwrap.","In Practice:

Before opening an item onto the sterile field, inspect the packaging to ensure no rips, tears, or damage to the packaging.

If opening a resterilized item (such as a pack of OR towels) make sure to inspect the steam indicators to ensure they have changed color.

Maintain a minimum 12” distance from the mayo stand when opening supplies to avoid contamination.","In VR:

Next, open the lid of the instrument tray by grasping the rings on top of the lid and then place the lid on top of the case cart.

Look inside and ensure that the steam indicators show that the contents have been exposed to steam as part of the sterilization process.

In Practice:
1. Avoid grabbing the lid from the edges, as this can increase the likelihood of accidentally contaminating the contents.
2. When inspecting the contents, maintain a minimum 12” distance from the sterilization tray to avoid contamination.
3. Similarly, inspect all packaging and filters for damage, as this can impact sterility. Holding items up to the light can help show any pinhole perforations in the material.

Click NEXT to advance.","In Practice:

Avoid grabbing the lid from the edges, as this can increase the likelihood of accidentally contaminating the contents.

When inspecting the contents, maintain a minimum 12” distance from the sterilization tray to avoid contamination.","In Practice:

Now that the initial setup is complete, you will perform a surgical scrub followed by gowning and gloving. These procedures are covered in a separate learning module.

Click NEXT to advance.","In Practice:

You are now scrubbed, gowned, and gloved and can continue with the back table setup.

Click NEXT to advance.","In VR:

["Welcome to the Patient Prep Skills Trainer module!

In this module we will focus on basic preoperative setup skills.  Our patient today will be undergoing an open appendectomy and you will be helping prepare him for surgery.  This patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies, and no previous surgical history.

In this tutorial, any instructions listed after “In VR:” should be completed within the training module.
Any information after “In Practice” is meant to provide additional information for real-world practice.

This module will cover the following skills:
• Hair Removal
• ESU Setup
• SCD Placement
• Patient Warming
• Skin Prep

Click NEXT to advance.","Because a patient is on the table, first ensure he is appropriately positioned and secured before proceeding. A patient should always be secured to the table with safety straps to prevent falls.

After you have confirmed the straps are in place, press Next to continue.","Hair Removal:

In Practice: In preparation for an appendectomy, any hair on the patient’s abdomen should be removed. This patient was already shaved in the pre-op area.  In general, this should be done outside of the Operating Room to prevent stray hair from contaminating other surfaces.  

Keep the following in mind during practice:

1. Check if hair removal is necessary. Only remove hair that might interfere with the procedure and keep hair in place whenever possible.
2. If hair needs to be removed, remove the smallest amount possible. Avoid flammable antiseptics in areas with a lot of hair.
3. When removing hair, do it outside the procedure room, like in a preoperative area. Use clippers or depilatories, and keep the patient warm and private.
 
Click NEXT to advance.","Hair Removal Continued:

4. Remove hair as close to the procedure time as possible to reduce infection risk.
5. Be careful not to nick the skin, especially on warts or moles, when using clippers.
6. Use electric or battery clippers—razors can increase the risk of infection.
7. Dispose of single-use clipper heads after one use, and clean reusable parts according to the manufacturer's instructions.
8. If hair removal must happen in the OR, wet clip or use a vacuum device to avoid contaminating sterile areas.
9. For depilatories, follow the manufacturer’s instructions. Test the depilatory on a small area at least 24 hours in advance to check for allergies or irritation.
 
Click NEXT to advance.","In VR: Now, let’s prepare the electrosurgical generator platform for the electrocautery device.  Grab the grounding pad out of the package and attach the pad to the patient’s right lateral thigh.

In Practice:
1. WIth any durable medical equipment such as the Bovie Pad / SCDs / Warming Blanket, it’s important to verify the expiration date before use.
2. Similarly, with any of these types of equipment, save the Lot and Expiration information for documentation purposes.
